test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 14 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following Acts provides legal status to Lok Adalats in India?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987** provides the legal framework for establishing Lok Adalats in India.
 
• Lok Adalats are also known as **"People's Court"**, which aim to provide inexpensive and expeditious justice.
 
• This Act ensures the **speedy resolution of disputes** and promotes the concept of amicable settlement.
 
• Under the Act, the decisions made by Lok Adalats are treated as **final and binding** on the parties involved.
 
• The Act empowers the Lok Adalats to deal with cases related to **civil, matrimonial, land, and labour disputes**, among others.
 
• Lok Adalats function under the supervision of the **National Legal Services Authority (NALSA)** and various State Legal Services Authorities.
 
• The Act guarantees legal aid to weaker sections of society, ensuring **equal access to justice**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Penal Code, 1860**__

 __
 
• The **Indian Penal Code (IPC)** is the main criminal code of India.
 
• It deals with crimes and penalties but does not address alternative dispute resolution mechanisms like Lok Adalats.
 
• It was enacted during British rule and is still in use with several amendments.
 
 
 
• **Civil Procedure Code, 1908**__
 __
 
• The **Civil Procedure Code (CPC)** governs the procedures for adjudication of civil cases in India.
 
• It does not specifically establish Lok Adalats, but it provides mechanisms for amicable resolution of disputes like mediation.
 
 
 
• **Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996**__
 
 
• This Act governs **arbitration and conciliation proceedings** in India.
 
• While it provides a framework for alternative dispute resolution, it is distinct from Lok Adalats and does not provide the legal status of Lok Adalats.
 
• It focuses primarily on commercial disputes and private arbitration.
